summary: Registered a follow-on sourced question (@q_restore_underflow_default_cfg) to settle how widely the just-asserted snapshot-trigger defect is reachable: the user-restore path sets last log/applied/snapshot to a burned index above the current log and then calls removeOldLogs for a monotonic log store, emptying the log while the snapshot index stays high - an independent producer of the same underflow that needs no caller-configured TrailingLogs. Recorded as a source-only interpretation (explained, no defect re-judged, since the existing assertion already covers the mechanism) with a discriminator that uses the snapshot's own MonotonicLogs cluster option with default TrailingLogs and SnapshotThreshold, sampling store last index, snapshot index, applied index and shouldSnapshot before and after the restore. Limitations note the untested restore-plus-monotonic-store state, that user restore is documented as disaster recovery rather than normal operation, and that a negative result would only narrow reachability.
